title: quant-stability-case-notes-jul2026
body:
Purpose
---
These are working notes summarizing a focused set of experiments on quantization stability: how output quality and latency vary across quant formats (INT8, AWQ, GPTQ, FP8) and across different kernel implementations. The emphasis here is on variance (stability) between runs and sensitivity to small runtime changes (batch size, seed, micro-batching), not just average throughput/latency.

Motivation / Problem statement
---
We repeatedly see runs where the average perplexity or downstream QA score is fine, but tail cases (rare prompts, longer contexts, or particular tokens) exhibit large divergence between quant schemes or kernels. This makes production rollouts risky: a canary looks good on typical prompts but fails on a small but important set. We want to quantify that instability and map root causes to actionable mitigations (calibration, fallback policies, kernel selection rules).

Experiment matrix (high level)
---
- Models: LLaMA-2-13B, Refined-Medium-7B (internal naming).
- Datasets / prompts: 1) question-answering set (50 curated hard prompts), 2) 200 random prompts from production logs, 3) 100 long-context prompts (1k tokens).
- Quant schemes: fp16 baseline, INT8 (symmetric per-channel), GPTQ (8-bit, learned quant with calibration), AWQ (approx per-tensor adaptive), FP8 (E4M3-like config).
- Kernels/implementations tested: default runtime kernel (fused attention), CUTLASS-style matmul, Triton-patched GEMM, and our in-house packed-kernel.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (pinned), H100-80GB (secondary), single-GPU runs for parity.
- Repeats: 8 independent runs per combination (different RNG seeds and micro-batching offsets). Collect per-run metrics and token-level divergence traces.

Metrics collected
---
- Latency: median, p95, p99 per request (end-to-end).
- Throughput: tokens/s (sustained over 60s window).
- Quality: perplexity delta vs fp16; top-1 token divergence rate (fraction of tokens differing from fp16); exact-match / answer accuracy on curated QA set; MAUVE proxy on a subset (coarse).
- Stability: inter-run stddev for perplexity and divergence rate; max-min spread across runs; number of runs with >5% token divergence.
- Profiling traces: kernel timings, memory allocs, KV cache stalls, memcpy times.

Key findings (summary)
---
1) AWQ shows consistently low average perplexity delta compared to fp16 across both models, but has higher inter-run variance when using the packed-kernel implementation (stddev of token-divergence ~2.1% vs 0.7% with CUTLASS). The instability correlates with micro-batch alignment — small changes in batch offsets cause different packing paths to be taken.

2) GPTQ has slightly larger median quality loss for the 13B model (perplexity +6-9%) but is extremely stable across runs and kernels (inter-run stddev ~0.4%). This makes GPTQ more predictable for canaries, even if average quality is worse vs AWQ.

3) INT8 symmetric per-channel performs well for throughput but exhibits infrequent large token divergences concentrated on rare tokens and long-context prompts. Profiling shows these cases often line up with attention key/cache boundary conditions where custom KV-cache code path triggers a memcpy + re-quant path; the memcpy latency sometimes races with kernel scheduling, introducing numerical nondeterminism on older CUDA drivers.

4) FP8 (emulation on A100) had near-zero quality delta for short contexts but lost ground on long contexts (perplexity +12% on 1k tokens). Latency was worse than INT8/GPTQ because FP8 paths are not well-optimized on our current fused-kernel stack (more conversions and slower matmuls).

5) Kernel-level differences matter more for AWQ and INT8 than for GPTQ. CUTLASS-style kernels gave more deterministic results; our packed-kernel yields higher throughput but can flip rounding decisions in the quant-dequant pipeline causing token divergence in edge cases.

Example reproduction (short recipe)
---
1) Checkout branch: benchmarks/quant-stability-exps (PR linked above).
2) Model: llama-2-13b-qat (fp16 checkpoint). Convert to AWQ with our calibration tool: ./convert_awq --calib-set /data/calib/2000.txt --heads-per-block 64
3) Run 8 seeds: for seed in {1..8}; do python run_bench.py --model awq-13b --kernel packed --batch 1 --max-tokens 256 --seed $seed --out results/$seed.json; done
4) Post-process: python analyze_stability.py results/*.json --compare-baseline fp16-13b.json --output stability-summary.csv

Profiling snippets / hints from traces
---
- Observed repeated small (~200us) memcpy spikes right before attention kernels in packed-kernel runs. These align with higher token divergence; when memcpy spikes are suppressed (redesigned allocator or pre-warm), divergence reduces.
- GPU occupancy for FP8 matmuls is lower on A100 (warps not fully utilized) causing higher latency variance. H100 shows better FP8 performance but we need to validate cost tradeoffs.
- Triton GEMM exhibited slightly fewer nondeterministic results vs packed-kernel; however its absolute throughput is lower for batch=1.

Root-cause hypotheses
---
- Packing-induced rounding path differences: when weights are packed into blocks, the accumulation order and quant-dequant steps differ slightly between kernels causing divergent rounding across tokens in low-probability branches.
- Memory allocator/async memcpy scheduling: sporadic memcpy timing changes can alter kernel launch timings; with fused-kernels and custom caching, this can flip deterministic order of reductions.
- Calibration sensitivity: AWQ's adaptive scales are more sensitive to the calibration sample distribution; small mismatches between calibration and production tokens amplify rare-token errors. GPTQ's learned quantizers generalize better at the cost of higher baseline error.

Immediate mitigations we tried
---
- Deterministic allocator + pinned memory for KV cache reduced memcpy spikes and reduced inter-run divergence by ~30% for packed-kernel + AWQ.
- Forced deterministic kernel launch order (synchronization around attention kernels) eliminated some flaky cases but increased latency p95 by ~8% — not acceptable for latency-SLO routes.
- Calibration augmentation for AWQ (add 10% of production-tail prompts) reduced rare-token divergence but at slight cost to mean perplexity on in-domain data.

Action items / next experiments
---
- Expand coverage: run same matrix on H100 and on Dedicated-hosted instance shapes to see whether hardware behavior explains some instability. (Owner: Aisha)
- Kernel rewrite: prototype a packed-kernel variant that preserves accumulation order equivalent to CUTLASS for blocks likely to contain rare-token-sensitive weights. (Owner: Marcus)
- Calibration policy: build a small pipeline to sample and auto-append tail prompts to AWQ calibration set before deployment. (Owner: Sofia)
- Canary policy: prefer GPTQ for initial canaries on new model+kernel combos due to stability, even if throughput is lower. Add automatic rollback when token-divergence > 3% on curated hard-set.

Notes to self / open questions
---
- Is there a cheap online metric we can compute per-request to flag potential quant-induced hallucination risk? (token-confidence-variance?)
- Should we adopt a hybrid policy: AWQ in steady-state for throughput, GPTQ for canary and fallback? Cost model needed.
- Need to validate with multi-GPU inference (pipeline-parallel) — packing behaviors may interact badly with sharding.

Appendix: raw numbers (high level)
---
- AWQ + packed-kernel (13B): median latency 340ms, p95 620ms, avg token-divergence 4.2%, inter-run stddev 2.1%
- GPTQ + CUTLASS (13B): median latency 370ms, p95 660ms, avg token-divergence 6.8%, inter-run stddev 0.4%
- INT8 + packed-kernel (13B): median latency 320ms, p95 700ms, avg token-divergence 3.6% but 2/8 runs had >8% divergence on long-context set
- FP8 (emulated) + Triton: median latency 410ms, p95 850ms, avg token-divergence 2.9% (but long-context delta +12% perplexity)

Concluding note
---
We should prioritize stability signals (inter-run variance and worst-case divergence on curated hard prompts) when selecting quant+kernel for production. AWQ offers promising average quality but current packed-kernel optimizations introduce instability that must be addressed (either through kernel changes or allocator/launch determinism). GPTQ is easier to reason about for safe rollouts. This doc is a snapshot — more systematic sweep (multiple hardware types, more seeds, production-tail sampling) recommended before policy changes.

-- Marcus
